findings.finding_summary: This systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials reported no benefit of resveratrol supplementation on C-reactive protein, total cholesterol, LDL cholesterol, triglycerides, or glucose.

findings.population: patients with metabolic syndrome and related disorders
findings.finding_summary: This meta-analysis reported significantly increased flow-mediated dilation with resveratrol supplementation in patients with metabolic syndrome and related disorders.

findings.population: patients with metabolic syndrome and related disorders
findings.finding_summary: The same meta-analysis reported no effect of resveratrol on systolic or diastolic blood pressure.

findings.endpoint: body weight, BMI, and waist circumference in type 2 diabetes
findings.finding_summary: This meta-analysis reported significant reductions in body weight, BMI, and waist circumference with resveratrol in type 2 diabetes, with no significant effect on hip circumference or waist-to-hip ratio.

findings.population: adults (mean age 58) across ten randomized trials
findings.finding_summary: This systematic review of ten randomized controlled trials (437 participants, 150-1200 mg/day, mean follow-up 9.6 weeks) reported an overall significant elevation of blood NAD levels with NMN supplementation, with no serious adverse effects observed.
findings.limitations: 437 participants across 10 trials; mean follow-up only 9.6 weeks

findings.population: adults (mean age 58) across ten randomized trials
findings.finding_summary: The same review reported that improvements in physical performance parameters with NMN were non-significant, and most clinically relevant outcomes did not differ from control despite the NAD elevation.
findings.limitations: 437 participants across 10 trials; grip strength moved only 29.9 to 30.5 kg

findings.finding_summary: In this randomized double-blind placebo-controlled trial, nicotinamide riboside at 100, 300, and 1000 mg daily dose-dependently increased whole-blood NAD+ by a reported 22%, 51%, and 142%, with no flushing and adverse-event rates similar to placebo.
findings.limitations: 8-week surrogate-endpoint trial in healthy overweight adults; no clinical outcomes measured

findings.finding_summary: This meta-analysis of 14 randomized controlled trials (2,149 patients) reported lower mortality with coenzyme Q10 versus placebo in heart failure (relative risk 0.69, 95% CI 0.50 to 0.95).
findings.limitations: heart-failure treatment context, adjunct to standard therapy — not a general-population longevity result

findings.finding_summary: The same meta-analysis reported greater improvement in exercise capacity with coenzyme Q10 than placebo, while left-ventricular ejection fraction showed no significant difference.

findings.population: overweight adults with newly diagnosed type 2 diabetes
findings.finding_summary: In this randomized trial of 753 overweight patients with newly diagnosed type 2 diabetes followed a median 10.7 years, intensive glucose control with metformin was associated with a 36% relative risk reduction in all-cause mortality and 42% in diabetes-related death versus conventional therapy.
findings.limitations: n=753; diabetes-treatment context — evidence does not establish longevity benefits in people without diabetes

findings.endpoint: long-term mortality and myocardial infarction (24-year post-trial follow-up)
findings.population: UKPDS participants followed up to 24 years
findings.finding_summary: This extended post-trial monitoring of the UKPDS reported that early intensive glycaemic control including metformin conferred a near-lifelong reduced risk of death and myocardial infarction compared with conventional control.
findings.limitations: post-trial observational follow-up of a diabetes trial; treatment allocation ended years earlier

findings.endpoint: visceral adiposity (primary outcome) and safety over 48 weeks
findings.finding_summary: In the PEARL randomized placebo-controlled trial of weekly low-dose compounded rapamycin (5 or 10 mg), visceral adiposity did not change significantly, and adverse and serious adverse events were similar across groups.
findings.limitations: compounded rapamycin (bioavailability differs from branded sirolimus); decentralized trial design

findings.endpoint: lean tissue mass in women (10 mg weekly)
findings.population: women in a healthy normative-aging cohort
findings.finding_summary: In the same trial, lean tissue mass and self-reported pain improved significantly for women taking 10 mg weekly rapamycin, and self-reported well-being improved at 5 mg.
findings.limitations: secondary outcomes in a sex-and-dose subgroup; primary outcome was null

findings.finding_summary: This meta-analysis of 17 randomized trials (896 participants) reported that quercetin lowered systolic blood pressure by a weighted mean 3.09 mmHg and diastolic by 2.86 mmHg versus control.
findings.limitations: 896 participants; effect sizes are small in absolute terms

findings.finding_summary: This earlier meta-analysis of 7 trials (587 participants) reported systolic and diastolic reductions with quercetin that were significant at doses of 500 mg/day and above, with no significant effect below 500 mg/day.
findings.limitations: the dose split is the load-bearing result: below 500 mg/day no significant effect was found

findings.endpoint: fasting blood glucose in prediabetes (primary outcome)
findings.finding_summary: In this randomized double-blind placebo-controlled trial (35 broccoli sprout extract, 39 placebo), the prespecified primary outcome was not met, with an overall 0.2 mmol/L fasting-glucose reduction; an exploratory subgroup with mild obesity and low insulin resistance showed a larger 0.4 mmol/L response.
findings.limitations: n=74; subgroup response is exploratory, not confirmatory

findings.endpoint: autism clinical impression scores in children (primary outcome)
findings.population: children aged 3-12 with autism spectrum disorder
findings.finding_summary: In this randomized double-blind placebo-controlled trial of 57 children, treatment effects of sulforaphane on the primary outcome (Ohio Autism Clinical Impressions Scale) were not significant versus placebo.
